ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient visit for recurrent fevers with chills after naval service in malaria-endemic areas, and an expected tropical deployment: history, examination, malaria testing, quantitative G6PD, and an infectious diseases (travel medicine) referral. Concerns: He fears another attack of fever at sea, where he would be far from a laboratory and responsible for the squadron; He must have every vaccine and certificate that entry to French Guiana and the islands requires before the squadron sails. [S]

tr.td: Chloroquine phosphate 500 mg tablet: 1,000 mg (two tablets) at once, then 500 mg at 6, 24 and 48 hours; take with food
1,000 mg, then 500 mg at 6, 24 and 48 hours (2,500 mg salt in total)
Primaquine phosphate 26.3 mg tablet (15 mg base): two tablets (30 mg base) by mouth daily with food for 14 days
30 mg base once daily for 14 days
Atovaquone-proguanil 250 mg/100 mg tablet: one tablet daily with food, starting one to two days before entering a malaria area, daily there, and for seven days after leaving
once daily from 1 to 2 days before until 7 days after the malaria areas
Azithromycin 500 mg tablet: one tablet daily for up to three days for severe travelers' diarrhea (standby supply)
once daily for up to 3 days if needed
Primaquine phosphate 26.3 mg tablet (15 mg base): two tablets (30 mg base) daily with food for 14 days, starting when he leaves the malaria areas (terminal prophylaxis)
30 mg base once daily for 14 days after leaving the malaria areas

list.item: Recurrent episodes of fever with shaking chills and drenching sweats, three in the past two years, each beginning months after naval service in malaria-endemic areas; the first diagnosed as malaria abroad on a blood smear with the species not recorded and treated with chloroquine alone, the later two treated with chloroquine without testing; the last ended six weeks before intake; afebrile and well at intake; cause not established at intake; infectious diseases consultation requested: resolved, confirmed [S]

Relapsing Plasmodium vivax malaria: P. vivax DNA detected by PCR in blood drawn between attacks, with negative smears and rapid antigen test; after three relapses treated without antirelapse therapy; normal quantitative G6PD: resolved, confirmed [S]

Small cutaneous abscess of the right forearm, about 2 cm, from a wooden splinter in the dockyard, without fever, spreading cellulitis or systemic signs; drained, without antibiotics; methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus on culture; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient visit for recurrent fevers with chills after naval service in malaria-endemic areas, and an expected tropical deployment: history, examination, malaria testing, quantitative G6PD, and an infectious diseases (travel medicine) referral
Two-week follow-up and infectious diseases consultation: PCR result and radical cure
Six-week review after chloroquine and primaquine: blood count, adverse effects, relapse surveillance
Pre-travel visit: yellow fever, hepatitis A, hepatitis B and typhoid vaccines, and the travel plan
Pre-departure review: no relapse, malaria chemoprophylaxis, vector, food and water precautions, standby treatment, and the plan on return
Same-day sick visit for a skin abscess of the right forearm

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Infectious diseases (travel medicine) consultation in two weeks to establish the cause of the recurrent fevers, advise on antirelapse treatment, and plan pre-travel care for the deployment

Malaria testing between attacks: thick and thin blood smears, rapid antigen test, and Plasmodium species PCR sent to the reference laboratory; quantitative G6PD activity before any primaquine; blood count, kidney and liver tests
Fever action plan: a blood smear the same day for any fever, at home, at sea or after travel; carry a card stating his malaria history

Chloroquine for the blood stage (1,000 mg salt, then 500 mg at 6, 24 and 48 hours) and primaquine 30 mg base daily for 14 days for radical cure, with the normal G6PD result; blood count and bilirubin after the course; report dark urine, breathlessness or blue lips

Pre-travel plan for French Guiana and the Antilles: one dose of yellow fever vaccine with the certificate, hepatitis A, hepatitis B if not immune, typhoid; atovaquone-proguanil chemoprophylaxis for malaria areas; repellent, permethrin-treated clothing, screened or air-conditioned quarters and bed nets against mosquitoes, fleas, lice and mites; food and water precautions with standby azithromycin; primaquine terminal prophylaxis after leaving the malaria areas, and a malaria test for any fever after return
GL-YB-YF-2026, GL-CDC-FG-2026, GL-YB-MAL-2026, GL-YB-DENGUE-2026, GL-YB-RICK-2026, GL-YB-TD-2026, GL-IDSA-TRAVEL-2006
No further malaria relapse in the six months after radical cure
No fever in the seven months since finishing primaquine
All required and recommended travel vaccines given, with a valid yellow fever certificate, at least ten days before departure
Yellow fever, hepatitis A dose 1, hepatitis B two-dose series, typhoid and influenza vaccines given; certificate valid
Knows to have a malaria test the same day for any fever, during travel and for months after return
Carries a fever card and explained the plan back correctly

list.item: Independent; lost about a week of work with each febrile attack [S]
